The [[R2-series astromech droid]] '''R2-SHP''', also known as "'''Shep'''," served the [[Resistance]] with his [[counterpart]] [[R6-LE5]] during the [[First Order-Resistance War|war]] against the [[First Order]]. The pair performed routine maintenance on the [[CR90 corvette]] ''[[Tantive IV]]'' while it was in the [[Resistance base (Ajan Kloss)|Resistance base]] on the [[moon]] [[Ajan Kloss]]. He was among those in the base who mourned the [[death]] of [[General]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] in [[35 ABY]].

==Biography==
R2-SHP, also known as "Shep," was an [[R2-series astromech droid]] who served in the [[Resistance]] during its [[First Order-Resistance War|war]] with the [[First Order]]. He and his [[counterpart]] [[R6-LE5]], who were considered "siblings," carried out routine maintenance on the [[CR90 corvette]] ''[[Tantive IV]]'' to ensure its function while it was used as the command hub of the [[Resistance base (Ajan Kloss)|Resistance base]] on the [[moon]] [[Ajan Kloss]].<ref name="TROS VD" />

In [[35 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|IX}} to [[35 ABY]].</ref> R2-SHP stood beneath the ''Tantive IV'' when the [[Jedi]] [[Jedi training|trainee]] [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] returned to the base from a training session and met with [[General]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], the Resistance's leader. With [[Lieutenant]] [[Kaydel Ko Connix]]'s assistance, Organa later passed by the [[Astromech droid|droid]] near the [[corvette]] in order to reach out to her [[Reproduction|son]], [[Ben Solo]], through [[the Force]].<ref name="TROS">{{Film|IX}}</ref>

[[File:LeiaFuneral-TROS.png|thumb|left|300px|R2-SHP (far right) mourned the loss of General Organa.]]
The general successfully communicated to her son with all her strength, but at the [[Death|cost]] of her life. R2-SHP was then among the large crowd that gathered around Organa's body to mourn in silence. The [[droid]] was again present near the ''Tantive IV'' when Organa's successor, General [[Poe Dameron]], learned that the [[planet]] [[Kijimi]] had been [[Destruction of Kijimi|destroyed]] by the [[Sith Eternal]] and listened to a [[The galaxy|galaxy]]-wide broadcast of theirs, which claimed that the Resistance had failed.<ref name="TROS" />

==Characteristics==
R2-SHP was more gregarious than R6-LE5 and rolled to help whereever he thought it was needed. As an older R2 unit, he had undergone frequent upgrading to stay contemporary and showed an earnestness that may have stemmed from a fear of obsolescence. The droid had [[Color|blue]] and silver plating, a black [[sensor]], and a blue logic function display.<ref name="TROS VD" /> R2-SHP stood 0.96 [[meter]] (3 [[Foot|feet]], 2 inches) tall<ref name="AEYNTK:UE" /> and was manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]].<ref name="Manufacturer" />

==Behind the scenes==
R2-SHP was created for the [[sequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']],<ref name="TROS" /> which was released in [[December]], [[2019]].<ref name="Jedi Redeemed">{{InsiderCite|196|The Jedi Redeemed: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker|The Jedi Redeemed: ''Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker''}}</ref> The droid was revealed beforehand in a [[Star Wars: Droid Factory (toy line)|''Star Wars: Droid Factory'']] pack of figures tied into the film and released by [[The Walt Disney Company]]<ref name="Toy">{{DisneyToyCite|set=Star Wars: Droid Factory (toy line)|packtype=Multipack|pack=D-O · R5-2JE · R6-LE5 · R2-SHP|link=star-wars-the-rise-of-skywalker-droid-factory-figure-set-400911413423.html}}</ref> in [[November]] 2019.<ref name="ToyDate">{{WebCite|url=https://www.jeditemplearchives.com/content/modules.php?name=JReviews&rop=showcontent&id=3855|text=D-O/R5-2JE/R6-LE5/R2-SHP - Droid Factory|author=Harrison, Paul|date=2019-12-12|work=[https://www.jeditemplearchives.com jeditemplearchives.com]|archivedate=20210116080954}}</ref> The droid was then identified as "Shep" in ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'', a reference book written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released alongside the film.<ref name="TROS VD" />

[[File:R2-SHP_Interior.jpg|thumb|right|250px|R2-SHP's head was removable to allow access to its interior.]]
The prop used for R2-SHP is predominantly made from aluminum, including an all-aluminum external shell as well as steel feet for durability. In order to be in keeping with the "used future" aesthetic established for ''[[Star Wars]]'' by director [[George Lucas]], R2-SHP was deliberately aged and distressed for usage in the film, and sustained further minor wear-and-tear during use. The prop is equipped with light up elements including its [[holoprojector]] and strips of LEDs on its dome that can cycle through various colors.<ref name="Prop">{{WebCite|url=https://usm.propstoreauction.com/m/lot-details/index/catalog/287/lot/73333|text=Lot # 344: Star Wars - EP IX - The Rise of Skywalker (2019) - R2-SHP Light-up Remote Control Droid|work=[https://usm.propstoreauction.com usm.propstoreauction.com]|archivedate=20210912083900}}</ref>

Controlled with a Spektrum™ DX6i remote control, the prop is also capable of turning its head and could move forward or backward as well as turn its position. R2-SHP's head was removable to allow access to the internal components, and during filming, the dome was swapped out with an R6 type head in order to create<ref name="Prop" /> R6-LE5<ref name="TROS VD" /> for additional scenes. The signature of [[Lee Towersey]], a lead droid technician on the film, can be found inside R2-SHP's dome. The dimensions of the prop are 75 centimeters by 70 centimeters by 110 centimeters (29.5 inches by 27.5 inches by 43.5 inches). In [[2021]], the prop sold at auction for $80,000.<ref name="Prop" />
